stimulus.text:
“That we being chiefly of the African extract, and by reason of long bondage and hard slavery, we have been deprived of enjoying the profits of our labor or the advantage of inheriting estates from our parents, as our neighbors the white people do. . . . Your petitioners further show, that we apprehend ourselves to be aggrieved, in that, while we are not allowed the privilege of freemen of the State, having no vote or influence in the election of those that tax us, yet many of our colour (as is well known) have cheerfully entered the field of battle in the defence of the common cause. . . .”
— Petition of Paul Cuffe, John Cuffe, and five others to the Massachusetts General Court, February 10, 1780 (abridged)

stem: The petitioners' central complaint is that they are

options.text: Forced to serve in the Continental Army against their will
options.misconception: The petitioners say the opposite: men of their color “cheerfully entered the field of battle,” and they cite that service as their claim.

options.text: Barred from owning any land in Massachusetts
options.misconception: They say they were “deprived of enjoying the profits of our labor”; the complaint is taxation without a vote, not a ban on owning land.

options.text: Denied the right to attend church with white neighbors
options.misconception: Church attendance never appears in the petition; the grievance is taxes and votes, not worship.

options.text: Taxed with no vote in choosing those who tax them

rationales.D: The petitioners state it plainly: “deprived of enjoying the profits of our labor,” they still have “no vote or influence in the election of those that tax us.”
rationales.A: They cite their wartime service proudly, as proof they deserve a voice; they never say they were forced to serve.
rationales.B: They do own small estates, which is why they are taxed; the grievance is the tax without the vote, not ownership.
rationales.C: Worship is not mentioned; the petition is about taxation, voting, and the rights of freemen.
rationales.general:
1. Read the grievance. Taxed while “deprived of enjoying the profits of our labor” after “long bondage and hard slavery.”
2. Read the missing half. “No vote or influence in the election of those that tax us.”
3. Add their proof. Men of their color fought “in the defence of the common cause” — service without a voice.
Remember: a complaint has two halves, the burden and the missing right — read both before answering.
